name: Alexander Hotel
positioning: Design-led hotel occupying several floors of the Torre Virreyes skyscraper in Lomas de Virreyes, across the street from Chapultepec park
best_for: Design-minded travelers who want park or skyline views from floor-to-ceiling windows
Travelers who want Chapultepec park and its museums right across the street

facts.text: Chapultepec park is directly across the street from the hotel.
Chapultepec park is home to the Museo Nacional de Antropologia, Museo Tamayo and Chapultepec Castle.
The neighborhood of Polanco is a five-minute drive away.
The hotel was designed by architect Daniel Alvarez Fernandez, with interiors by Lorena Cherem and Linda Masri of Ambia Studio.
Contemporary artworks curated by Nicole Badin are integrated throughout the hotel.
The spa has private treatment rooms and steam cabins.
The gym offers private sessions with a trainer, a jogging coach and a yoga instructor.
A lifestyle concierge can arrange experiences such as a tour of Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul or a private driver to Teotihuacan.
E-bikes are available for guests to borrow.
All suites and common areas are wheelchair-accessible via glass elevators.
The hotel is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World and is operated by Namron Hospitality Group.

highlights.text: The hotel occupies several floors of Torre Virreyes, one of the final works of Mexican modernist architect Teodoro Gonzalez de Leon.
The Alexander Suite has a 180-degree view of Chapultepec Park through expansive windows, plus a deep soaking tub and rain shower.
All rooms have king beds and floor-to-ceiling windows that open toward either the skyline or Chapultepec.
Rooms have blue calcite marble bathrooms, dark ebony wood and leather accents, Bang & Olufsen speakers and Byredo toiletries.
The hotel has a Petrossian caviar bar.

considerations.text: Lomas de Virreyes is a financial district and residential pocket that isn't necessarily a walking neighborhood; it is mostly surrounded by embassies and law firms rather than cafes or galleries.
The bathrooms are glass-walled, with a heavy curtain for privacy.
The hotel is technically family-friendly, but the aesthetic skews strongly toward adults.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Alexander Hotel review
